jobs.name: ATLAS daily sync
jobs.prompt:
Run the ATLAS backup script and report results.

Execute: bash ~/.hermes/scripts/atlas-sync.sh

This script:
1. Backs up skills, memories (MEMORY.md, USER.md), sanitized config, safe env vars, cron jobs, scripts to ~/ProG/ATLAS/_hermes_backups/TODAY/
2. Encrypts .env, config.yaml, auth.json with GPG to ~/ProG/ATLAS/_secrets/ (LOCAL ONLY, never pushed)
3. Syncs newer skills to ATLAS repo
4. Runs pre-commit secret scan (blocks push if secrets detected)
5. Pushes to github.com:BongweKE/ATLAS.git
6. Mirrors to ml-ke repo (legacy)

Report: how many skills backed up, whether secrets encrypted OK, and whether push succeeded.

jobs.name: blog-poster
jobs.prompt:
PUBLISH ONE BLOG POST — handles date rewriting

TODAY=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
cd /home/pro-g/ProG/ml-ke

# Check for today's scheduled post
MATCH=$(ls .scheduled/${TODAY}-*.md 2>/dev/null | head -1)

if [ -n "$MATCH" ]; then
  mv "$MATCH" _posts/
  BASENAME=$(basename "$MATCH")
  git add "_posts/$BASENAME"
  git commit -m "Publish: $BASENAME"
  git pull --rebase origin main
  git push origin main
  echo "PUBLISHED: $BASENAME"
  exit 0
fi

# No match for today — take first remaining, rewrite its date
FIRST=$(ls .scheduled/*.md 2>/dev/null | head -1)
if [ -z "$FIRST" ]; then
  echo "All posts published! Nothing to do."
  exit 0
fi

BASENAME=$(basename "$FIRST")
OLD_DATE=$(echo "$BASENAME" | grep -oP '^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}')

# Rewrite front matter date and rename file to today
sed -i "s/date: $OLD_DATE/date: $TODAY/" "$FIRST"
NEW_NAME=$(echo "$BASENAME" | sed "s/$OLD_DATE/$TODAY/")

mv "$FIRST" "_posts/$NEW_NAME"
git add "_posts/$NEW_NAME"
git commit -m "Publish (date-fixed): $NEW_NAME"
git pull --rebase origin main
git push origin main
echo "PUBLISHED (date-fixed): $NEW_NAME"

jobs.name: tuesday-ai-update
jobs.prompt:
Write the weekly AI Update blog post for the ML Kenya blog (ml.co.ke). This is a TUESDAY feature — the post should cover fresh AI developments from the past week.

DATE: Today is $(date +%Y-%m-%d) which is a Tuesday. Write the post with this date in front matter.

WORKFLOW (follow exactly):
1. cd ~/ProG/ml-ke && git pull origin main
2. Run MULTIPLE web_search queries to gather fresh content. Search for:
   - "AI news this week" 
   - Then region-specific searches: "China AI", "Europe AI", "Africa AI", "MENA AI", "South America AI", "Russia AI"
   - Search for specific companies: DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu/Z.AI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, Microsoft AI, SpaceXAI/Grok, G42/Core42
3. After gathering web results, write a post to _posts/$(date +%Y-%m-%d)-tuesday-ai-update.md
   - Title format: "Tuesday AI Update: [Date] — [Top story headline]"
   - Categories: [AI Engineering, AI in Africa]
   - Tags: [tuesday-update, WEEK-MONTH-YEAR, ai-news]
   - Cover: reuse /assets/img/cover-global-ai-roundup-july-2026.webp as generic cover for now
   - Keep it 600-900 words — concise and useful
   - Structure: 1-2 paragraphs intro → region-by-region highlights (bullet points) → "Spotlight" section on one major story → "Why This Matters for Africa" section
   
4. git add, commit with message "Add post: Tuesday AI Update $(date +%Y-%m-%d)", and push

IMPORTANT: Every fact must come from a web search result. If search returns nothing for a region, skip it. Do NOT invent facts. Do NOT use {% post_url %} tags. Use markdown links like /posts/slug/ for internal links or full URLs for external sources.
